mainTopic: The second day of ראש השנה, baking thick bread on יום טוב, and רבן גמליאל's leniencies about sweeping and incense, including smoking fruit over coals.
overview: The amud opens at the end of a challenge to אמימר. אמימר answers that he follows the scholars of נהרדעא: the second day of ראש השנה is like any second day of יום טוב, even for an egg, since אלול has not been made thirty days long since עזרא's time. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's rule that only thin loaves are baked on יום טוב. רב הונא measures 'thick bread' as one טפח, based on the לחם הפנים. רב יוסף objects that the Temple's baking conditions were very different. רב then explains that 'thick bread' really means a large batch, which is forbidden on any יום טוב because of needless effort, and a ברייתא supports this. A new משנה lists three leniencies of רבן גמליאל: sweeping, incense, and a whole-roasted kid on פסח night. A ברייתא about רבן גמליאל's household forces the גמרא to restate רב אסי: the argument is about incense for its smell, and perfuming clothes is forbidden by everyone. Finally, the גמרא discusses smoking fruit with spices, and רב הונא explains that it both puts out and lights the coals.

steps.title: The challenge ends: an egg is different
steps.stepSummary: The challenger finishes his argument: the leniency for the second day of ראש השנה (for burial) does not apply to an egg laid on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which is not the case regarding an egg!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of a challenge that began on the previous page. It says that for an egg, the two days of ראש השנה are treated as one day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenger argues that the two days of ראש השנה count as one long holy day. Burial on the second day was allowed only out of respect for the dead. That special leniency should not spread to other matters, like an egg laid on the first day.

keyTerms.meaning: An egg. Here it means an egg laid on יוֹם טוֹב, which is forbidden to eat that day.
Which is not so. Used to show that one case differs from another.

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new statement. It closes an argument that started on the previous page, about whether the second day of ראש השנה is treated as a separate day.

phrases.english: Which is not so with regard to an egg!
phrases.notes: He means an egg laid on the first day of ראש השנה: it stays forbidden on the second day too, because the two days count as one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a challenge begun before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's position that the second day of ראש השנה can be treated leniently like the second day of other holidays.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The burial leniency is a special exception made out of respect for the dead. In general, including for an egg, the two days of ראש השנה are one long day.

steps.title: אמימר follows the scholars of נהרדעא
steps.stepSummary: אמימר answers that he holds like נהרדעי, who say the second day of ראש השנה is like any second day of יום טוב, even regarding an egg.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I hold like the scholars of נהרדעא, who say this even regarding an egg.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר defends himself by saying he follows a different opinion. In that view, the egg case also follows the lenient rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that everyone agrees an egg is treated strictly. אמימר replies that the scholars of נהרדעא disagree: for them, the second day of ראש השנה is like the second day of other holidays, egg included. So his practice is consistent.

keyTerms.meaning: The scholars of נְהַרְדְּעָא, a major Torah center in Babylonia.
I hold, meaning that is my opinion.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is אמימר answering the challenger.

phrases.english: I hold in accordance with the scholars of Neharde'a,
who say it even with regard to an egg.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relying on a different opinion (נהרדעי) that rejects the challenger's starting assumption.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The egg case proves that the two days of ראש השנה are one long day.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to נהרדעי, even an egg follows the rule of a regular second day of יום טוב.

steps.title: The worry about a thirty-day אלול is groundless
steps.stepSummary: אמימר asks what the worry could be: that אלול might be made thirty days long? He answers with רב חיננא בר כהנא, who said that since עזרא's time אלול was never made thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is your reasoning? That perhaps they will make אלול a thirty-day month? But רב חיננא בר כהנא said: from the days of עזרא onward, we have not found a thirty-day אלול.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר names the reason behind the strict view and then knocks it down. He uses a statement of רב חיננא בר כהנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strict view might worry that if אלול had thirty days, the second day would be the real first day of תשרי, which is the true ראש השנה. רב חיננא בר כהנא reports that since עזרא, אלול was always twenty-nine days. So the first day is the real ראש השנה, and the second day is only a custom-based extra day.

keyTerms.meaning: What is your reasoning? What are you thinking?
They extend, meaning they make a month full with thirty days.
A 'full' אֱלוּל of thirty days instead of twenty-nine.
From the days of עֶזְרָא onward.

steps.whatToRemember: אמימר follows נהרדעי: the second day of ראש השנה is like any second day of יום טוב. The worry that it might be the real ראש השנה falls away, because since עזרא אלול was never made thirty days.

phrases.english: And what is your reasoning?
That perhaps they will make Elul a full month?
phrases.notes: If אלול had thirty days, the second day of ראש השנה would really be the first of תשרי.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Chinnana bar Kahana say:
From the days of Ezra and onward
we have not found a full Elul.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי דַּעְתָּיךְ דִּלְמָא מְעַבְּרִי לֵיהּ לֶאֱלוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up step 2 by removing the reason behind the challenger's strictness.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reasoning behind treating the two days of ראש השנה as one long day.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The worry that אלול might be made thirty days long has no basis, since that has not happened since עזרא's time.

steps.title: The משנה: only thin loaves may be baked
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that on יום טוב one does not bake thick loaves, only thin ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may not bake thick loaves, only thin ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. This sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line comes from the previous משנה's list of three things where רבן גמליאל was strict, following בית שמאי: on יום טוב one bakes only thin loaves. The גמרא will look for the source and the exact meaning of 'thick'.

phrases.english: And one may not bake thick loaves
but only thin ones.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה, about baking on יום טוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין אוֹפִין פִּתִּין גְּרִיצִין אֶלָּא רְקִיקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ראש השנה discussion and starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב one bakes only thin loaves, not thick ones.

steps.title: A ברייתא: בית שמאי and בית הלל on thick bread for פסח
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that בית שמאי forbid baking thick bread on פסח, and בית הלל permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: בית שמאי say one may not bake thick bread on פסח, and בית הלל permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related ברייתא about thick bread. It shows a מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Thick dough takes longer to bake through, so בית שמאי worry it may become חמץ. בית הלל are not worried and permit it. This sets up the question of how thick 'thick' is.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: Beit Shammai say:
one may not bake thick bread on Passover,
and Beit Hillel permit it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא on the related subject of thick bread.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי forbid thick bread on פסח, and בית הלל permit it.

steps.title: How thick is 'thick bread'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what thickness counts as 'thick bread' that בית הלל permit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is thick bread?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a measurement. This sets up רב הונא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל allow thick bread, but there must be a limit. The question asks how thick a loaf can be and still be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: And how much? Used to ask for a measurement.

phrases.english: And how much is thick bread?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact limit of the permission in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The maximum thickness of bread that בית הלל permit on פסח.

steps.title: רב הונא: one טפח, as with the לחם הפנים
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says the limit is one טפח. He learns this from the לחם הפנים, which was one טפח thick and still did not become חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: a טפח. For so we find with the לחם הפנים: a טפח.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives the measurement and a source for it. The source is the bread in the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לחם הפנים had to be מצה, and it was a טפח thick. So a טפח-thick loaf can be baked without becoming חמץ. רב הונא applies the same limit to regular bread.

keyTerms.meaning: A handbreadth, roughly the width of four fingers.
The showbread, twelve loaves placed on the שֻׁלְחָן in the בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ.
For so we find. Introduces a comparison or source.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: A handbreadth.
For so we find with the showbread: a handbreadth.
phrases.notes: The לחם הפנים was a טפח thick and had to be מצה, so that thickness clearly doesn't have to become חמץ.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One טפח, based on the thickness of the לחם הפנים.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the לחם הפנים is not a fair comparison
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף objects: the לחם הפנים was made by careful כהנים and was well-kneaded. Ordinary bread is made by less careful people and is less kneaded.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף strongly objected: if they said it about careful people, would they say it about people who are not careful? If they said it about well-kneaded bread, would they say it about bread that is not well-kneaded?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks רב הונא's comparison. He gives two differences between the לחם הפנים and regular bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, the כהנים were careful and made sure the dough did not turn חמץ, while ordinary people are not as careful. Second, the לחם הפנים was kneaded very well, which slows leavening, while home bread is not. So a טפח being safe in the בית המקדש does not prove it is safe at home.

keyTerms.meaning: Strongly objects to it. A firm challenge.
Careful, quick people. Here it means the כֹּהֲנִים.

steps.whyThisMatters: רב יוסף's two points show that a proof from the בית המקדש may not carry over to regular homes, where conditions are different.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef strongly objects to it:
If they said it regarding careful people,
phrases.notes: He means the כהנים who baked the לחם הפנים.

phrases.english: would they say it regarding people who are not careful?
If they said it regarding well-kneaded bread,
would they say it regarding bread that is not well-kneaded?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's source in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's comparison between regular bread and the לחם הפנים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The לחם הפנים had two safeguards that regular bread lacks: careful כהנים and thorough kneading. So its safe thickness cannot be applied to ordinary bread.

steps.title: Temple ovens and wood were different too
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף adds three more differences between baking in the בית המקדש and baking at home: dry wood versus moist wood, a hot oven versus a cold one, and a metal oven versus a clay one.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the rule was said about dry wood, would it be said about moist wood? If it was said about a hot oven, would it be said about a cold oven? If it was said about a metal oven, would it be said about a clay oven?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף keeps attacking רב הונא's proof from the לחם הפנים. He shows that the Temple's baking conditions were much faster than ordinary home baking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bread becomes חמץ when it sits or bakes slowly. In the בית המקדש, dry wood, a very hot oven and a metal oven all baked the bread fast, so a טפח-thick loaf had no time to become חמץ. At home, the wood is moist, the oven is cooler and it is made of clay, so a loaf that thick could become חמץ.

keyTerms.meaning: dry wood, which burns hot and fast

phrases.english: If they said it with dry wood,
phrases.notes: 'It' means the idea that a טפח-thick loaf won't become חמץ, which was learned from the Temple bread.

phrases.english: would they say it with moist wood?
If they said it with a hot oven,
would they say it with a cold oven?
If they said it with a metal oven,
would they say it with a clay oven?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם אָמְרוּ בְּעֵצִים יְבֵשִׁים יֹאמְרוּ בְּעֵצִים לַחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב יוסף's objection from step 8 with three more differences.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's proof from the לחם הפנים (step 7)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Baking in the Temple was much faster than baking at home, so what was safe there proves nothing about ordinary bread.

steps.title: Thick bread means a lot of bread
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה בר אבא reports that he privately asked his teacher, רב, and was told that 'פת עבה' means a large quantity of bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה בר אבא said: I asked my teacher privately, and who was he? רב. I asked: what is 'thick bread'? He answered: a large amount of bread.
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of measuring thickness, the גמרא gives a new answer to the question from step 6: 'thick bread' really means a big batch of bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This takes the whole topic away from the fear of חמץ. Now the problem is that baking a big batch is too much work on יום טוב. So רב יוסף's objections about the Temple ovens no longer matter.

phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said:
I asked my teacher in private,
phrases.notes: Here 'רבי' means 'my teacher', not רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: and who is he? Rav:
What is 'thick bread'?
A large amount of bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב יוסף has weakened רב הונא's answer, a whole new meaning of 'thick bread' is offered.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It means a large quantity of bread, not bread that is physically thick.
steps.whyThisMatters: It changes the reason for the rule from fear of חמץ to too much effort on יום טוב, and this sets up the question in step 14.

steps.title: Another version: רב heard it from רבינו הקדוש
steps.stepSummary: A second version says רב ירמיה בר אבא quoted רב, and that רב was the one who asked his own teacher, רבינו הקדוש. The answer is the same: a large amount of bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רב ירמיה בר אבא said in the name of רב: I asked my teacher privately, and who was he? רבינו הקדוש. What is 'thick bread'? A large amount of bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of who asked whom. The answer does not change.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, רב is the one who asked, and the explanation goes back one generation earlier, to his teacher רבי יהודה הנשיא. The answer itself is the same.

keyTerms.meaning: our holy teacher, a title for רבי יהודה הנשיא

phrases.english: Some say:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said that Rav said:
I asked my teacher in private,
and who is he? Our holy Rabbi:
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה הנשיא, רב's teacher.

phrases.english: What is 'thick bread'? A large amount of bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second version of step 10 with a different chain of who said it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Same answer: פת עבה means פת מרובה.

steps.title: Why call a big batch 'thick'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a large amount of bread would be called 'thick bread'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do they call it 'thick bread'?
steps.whatsHappening: The new meaning does not match the plain words, so the גמרא asks why that word was used. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'עבה' normally means thick, not many. If it really means a large amount, the wording needs an explanation.

phrases.english: And why do they call it 'thick bread'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the wording of the new meaning given in steps 10 and 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the word 'thick' is used for a large quantity.

steps.title: Two reasons for the name
steps.stepSummary: Either a big batch of dough looks thick when it is kneaded, or in that תנא's area people simply called a large amount 'thick bread'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is big when it is kneaded. Or: in the place where this תנא lived, a large amount of bread was called 'thick bread'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two possible reasons why the word 'thick' fits a large batch of bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reason is about how it looks: a large mass of dough is thick while it is being kneaded. The second reason is about local language: that was simply what people called it where this תנא lived.

phrases.english: Because it is large at the kneading.
Alternatively, in the place of this tanna,

phrases.aramaic: פַּת מְרוּבָּה — פַּת עָבָה קָרוּ לֵיהּ
phrases.english: a large amount of bread is called 'thick bread'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A big batch looks thick when kneaded, or 'thick' was the local word for a large amount.

steps.title: Then why mention only פסח?
steps.stepSummary: If the problem is unnecessary effort, it should apply to every יום טוב, so why does the ברייתא mention פסח?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, since the reason is that he works hard without needing to, why mention פסח in particular? It should apply to the other ימים טובים too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from step 5: under the new meaning, there is no reason to single out פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mentioning פסח made sense when the worry was חמץ. Now the worry is too much work, and that is true on any יום טוב. So naming פסח seems out of place.

phrases.english: Now, since it is because he exerts himself
with effort that is not needed,
why mention פסח specifically?
Even on the other Festivals too!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדִי מִשּׁוּם דְּקָטָרַח טִרְחָא דְּלָא צְרִיךְ הוּא מַאי אִרְיָא פֶּסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the new meaning from steps 10 and 11 to question the wording of the ברייתא in step 5.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the reason is extra effort, the rule is not special to פסח, so the ברייתא should not limit it to פסח.

steps.title: True, but the תנא was talking about פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that the rule applies to every יום טוב. The תנא mentioned פסח only because that was the topic he was discussing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is true. But the תנא was dealing with the יום טוב of פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge and explains that naming פסח was not meant to limit the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mention of פסח comes from the setting of the discussion, not from the law itself. The rule really applies to every יום טוב.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not conclude that baking a big batch is allowed on other ימים טובים. The rule is the same for all of them; פסח was mentioned only because it was the topic.

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so.
But the tanna was dealing with the Festival of Passover.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the point and explains that the wording comes from the setting of the discussion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mentioning פסח suggested the rule is special to פסח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule applies to every יום טוב; פסח was mentioned only because it was the topic.

steps.title: A ברייתא says it about every יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records the same disagreement using 'פת מרובה' and 'יום טוב' in general: בית שמאי forbid it and בית הלל permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also taught in a ברייתא: בית שמאי say one may not bake a large amount of bread on יום טוב, and בית הלל permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports both new points: the topic is a large amount of bread, and it applies to any יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא says 'פת מרובה' instead of 'פת עבה', and 'יום טוב' instead of 'פסח'. That confirms both the new meaning and the answer in step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: it was also taught this way (a supporting ברייתא)

steps.whatToRemember: In the end, 'פת עבה' means a large batch of bread. בית שמאי forbid baking it on any יום טוב because of unnecessary effort, and בית הלל permit it.

phrases.english: It was also taught so:
Beit Shammai say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אוֹפִין פַּת מְרוּבָּה בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: One may not bake a large amount of bread on a Festival,
and Beit Hillel permit it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports steps 10, 11 and 15 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That פת עבה means פת מרובה and that the rule applies to every יום טוב
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the בית שמאי and בית הלל disagreement about פת מרובה on יום טוב

steps.title: Three more leniencies of רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists three things רבן גמליאל permitted, and the חכמים forbid all three.
steps.simpleTranslation: He (רבן גמליאל) also said three things to be lenient. One may sweep the dining room. One may put incense on coals on יום טוב. One may make a whole-roasted kid on the night of פסח. The חכמים forbid all three.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It lists three cases where רבן גמליאל was lenient and the חכמים disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous משנה gave cases where רבן גמליאל was strict. Here the משנה gives the opposite: three leniencies. The three cases are sweeping the room where people eat, burning incense, and roasting a young goat whole on פסח night. The חכמים forbid all three.

keyTerms.meaning: the room of couches, the dining room
incense: fragrant spices put on burning coals

steps.whatToRemember: Three leniencies of רבן גמליאל: sweeping, incense, and a whole-roasted kid. The חכמים forbid all three.

phrases.english: MISHNA

phrases.aramaic: אַף הוּא אָמַר שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים לְהָקֵל:
phrases.english: He too said three things to be lenient:
phrases.notes: "He" is רבן גמליאל, from the previous משנה.

phrases.english: One may sweep the room of the couches
phrases.notes: This is the dining room, where people reclined on couches to eat.

phrases.english: and one may place incense on a Festival
and one may prepare a whole-roasted kid
on the nights of Passover.
And the Sages forbid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף הוּא אָמַר שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים לְהָקֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה. It moves from רבן גמליאל's strict rulings to his lenient ones.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל permits sweeping, incense, and a whole-roasted kid. The חכמים forbid them.

steps.title: רב אסי limits the incense argument
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי says the incense argument is only about perfuming things. Burning incense just to enjoy the smell is allowed by everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: The argument is about perfuming. But to smell it, everyone agrees it is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי explains which kind of incense burning the משנה is arguing about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using smoke to perfume clothes or objects is not a bodily enjoyment. That is the case רבן גמליאל and the חכמים argue about. Burning incense just to enjoy the smell is a personal pleasure, like food, so even the חכמים allow it on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: to perfume (clothes or objects) with incense smoke
to smell, to enjoy the scent

steps.confusionAlert: רב אסי does not say all incense is allowed. He says the argument is only about perfuming. Enjoying the smell is allowed by everyone.

phrases.english: GEMARA
Rav Asi said:
The dispute is about perfuming,
but to enjoy the smell
all agree it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the exact case of the משנה's incense argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument is only about perfuming. Burning incense to enjoy the smell is permitted by all.

steps.title: A ברייתא about sweeping in רבן גמליאל's house
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רב אסי. Its first part says sweeping is forbidden on יום טוב. רבי אליעזר בר צדוק reports that רבן גמליאל's house actually swept the day before.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged רב אסי from a ברייתא. One may not sweep the dining room on יום טוב, but רבן גמליאל's house would sweep. רבי אליעזר בר צדוק said: many times I went with my father into רבן גמליאל's house. They did not sweep on יום טוב. They swept on ערב יום טוב and covered the floor with sheets. The next day, when guests came, they took off the sheets, and the room was already clean. The חכמים said to him: if so, this is allowed even on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge against רב אסי by quoting a ברייתא. This first part is about sweeping; the incense part, which matters for the challenge, comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first gives the plain rule: no sweeping on יום טוב, though רבן גמליאל's house did sweep. רבי אליעזר בר צדוק says that even there, the sweeping was really done before יום טוב. The חכמים answer that such a setup is fine even on שבת, so it is not a special יום טוב leniency at all.

keyTerms.meaning: swept by itself (already clean, with nothing done on the day)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְכַבְּדִין בֵּית הַמִּטּוֹת בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: One may not sweep the room of the couches on a Festival,
but those of Rabban Gamliel's house would sweep.
Rabbi Eliezer bar Tzadok said:
Many times I went in after Father,
into Rabban Gamliel's house,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הָיוּ מְכַבְּדִין בֵּית הַמִּטּוֹת בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: and they would not sweep the room of the couches on the Festival,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מְכַבְּדִין אוֹתָן מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: rather they swept them on the eve of the Festival,
and spread sheets over them.
The next day, when guests came in,
they removed the sheets
and the house turned out to be swept by itself.
They said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, אַף בַּשַּׁבָּת מוּתָּר לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן.
phrases.english: If so, even on Shabbat it is permitted to do so.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי אֵין מְכַבְּדִין בֵּית הַמִּטּוֹת בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge against רב אסי's statement by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's claim that burning incense for its smell is permitted by all
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The challenge rests on the ברייתא's incense clause, which comes next. This sweeping section is the opening part of the same ברייתא.

steps.title: The same ברייתא about incense in רבן גמליאל's house
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא goes on: incense may not be placed on יום טוב, though רבן גמליאל's house did. רבי אליעזר בר צדוק reports that they really filled closed iron pans with smoke before יום טוב and opened them for guests.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not place incense on יום טוב, but רבן גמליאל's house would. רבי אליעזר בר צדוק said: many times I went with my father into רבן גמליאל's house. They did not place incense on יום טוב. Instead, they brought iron pans with holes. They filled them with smoke on ערב יום טוב and plugged the holes. The next day, when guests came, they opened the holes, and the house was perfumed by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the ברייתא, now on incense. This is the part it will use against רב אסי, and the actual challenge is spelled out right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא states flatly that incense is forbidden on יום טוב. It does not say this applies only to perfuming. The incense was opened for guests to enjoy the smell. That looks like the very case רב אסי said everyone permits, and this is the tension the גמרא will press next.

keyTerms.meaning: iron pans with holes for holding incense smoke

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבן גמליאל's household broke the rule. According to רבי אליעזר בר צדוק, everything was prepared before יום טוב; on the day they only opened the holes.
steps.whyThisMatters: This clause, which forbids incense on יום טוב with no limit, is what the גמרא will use to test רב אסי's claim that burning incense for its smell is allowed by all.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מַנִּיחִין אֶת הַמּוּגְמָר בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: And one may not place incense on a Festival,
but those of Rabban Gamliel's house would place it.
Rabbi Eliezer bar Tzadok said:

phrases.aramaic: פְּעָמִים הַרְבֵּה נִכְנַסְתִּי אַחַר אַבָּא לְבֵית רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: Many times I went in after Father into Rabban Gamliel's house,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הָיוּ מַנִּיחִין אֶת הַמּוּגְמָר בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: and they would not place incense on the Festival,
rather they brought perforated coal pans of iron
and filled them with smoke on the eve of the Festival,
and plugged their holes on the eve of the Festival.
The next day, when guests came in,
they opened their holes
and the house turned out to be perfumed by itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין מַנִּיחִין אֶת הַמּוּגְמָר בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא. This is the incense clause the challenge depends on.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's claim that burning incense for its smell is permitted by all
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids incense on יום טוב with no limit, and the incense in the story was for guests to smell. This seems to show the argument covers smelling too, against רב אסי.

steps.title: The חכמים answer: then it would be allowed even on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer רבי אליעזר בר צדוק that if filling pans before יום טוב makes it okay, then it should be allowed on שבת too. This finishes the challenge against רב אסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: If so, it should be allowed to do this on שבת as well.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the ברייתא from Step 20. It completes the גמרא's challenge to רב אסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים do not forbid the pan method. They say it is so harmless that it would be allowed even on שבת, so it cannot be רבן גמליאל's special leniency. That means his real leniency, which the ברייתא's opening line forbids, was placing incense on יום טוב to make the house smell nice for guests. So the argument is about smelling, against רב אסי's claim that everyone allows it.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if your reasoning is correct

phrases.english: They said to him: If so,
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבי אליעזר בר צדוק, who explained that the pans were filled before יום טוב.

phrases.english: it should be permitted to do so on Shabbos as well.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אִם כֵּן, אַף בַּשַּׁבָּת מוּתָּר לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא quoted in Steps 19-20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's statement in Step 18 that everyone allows burning incense just for the smell.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים say the pan method would be allowed even on שבת, so רבן גמליאל's leniency must have been actually placing incense on יום טוב for the house's smell. The ברייתא's opening line forbids that, so the argument covers smelling, against רב אסי.

steps.title: רב אסי's statement is restated the other way around
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes its version of רב אסי. The argument is about burning incense for the smell, and perfuming clothes is forbidden by everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if this was said, it was said like this: רב אסי said: The argument is about smelling, but perfuming clothes is forbidden by everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge. It says רב אסי's words must have been said differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the old version, smelling was allowed by everyone and the argument was about perfuming. In the new version it is the reverse. The argument between רבן גמליאל and the חכמים is about smelling, and perfuming clothes is forbidden by all. This fits the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said (a formula for restating a teaching)
To smell; to make a nice scent in the room
To perfume something, such as clothes, with incense smoke

steps.whatToRemember: In the final version of רב אסי, perfuming clothes on יום טוב is forbidden by everyone. The argument is only about burning incense for its smell.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix the two versions. The new version flips the old one: now smelling is the argued case, and perfuming is forbidden by everyone.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was stated,
this is how it was stated:
Rav Asi said:
the dispute is about burning it for the smell,
but to perfume, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 21 by restating רב אסי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Restating the teaching in a different way
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone allows burning incense for the smell, and the argument is only about perfuming.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is about smelling, and perfuming clothes is forbidden by everyone.

steps.title: May one smoke fruit with spices on יום טוב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks a new question: is it allowed to smoke fruit with spices on יום טוב to give it a nice smell?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: what is the law about smoking?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about smoking. This sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the smoke is used for food, not just for a room or for clothes. It might count as getting food ready, which is allowed on יום טוב, or it might not.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the scholars
To smoke; to put spices on coals so the smoke gives fruit a nice smell

phrases.english: A question was raised before them: What is the law about smoking?
phrases.notes: He means smoking fruit with spices on coals to give it a nice smell.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from incense for smell to smoking food.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether smoking fruit with spices on יום טוב is allowed.

steps.title: רב forbids it and שמואל permits it
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה בר אבא quotes רב that smoking fruit is forbidden. שמואל says it is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה בר אבא said in the name of רב: It is forbidden. And שמואל said: It is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two opposite answers to the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב and שמואל disagree about smoking fruit on יום טוב. At this point, neither one gives a reason.

phrases.aramaic: רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב: אָסוּר.
phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said that Rav said: It is forbidden.
And Shmuel said: It is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב: אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב says it is forbidden. שמואל says it is allowed.

steps.title: רב הונא: it is forbidden because it puts out coals
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says smoking is forbidden because the spices put out some of the burning coals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: It is forbidden, because one puts out fire.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא also says smoking is forbidden, and he gives a reason for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the spice powder is sprinkled on the coals, some of them go out. Putting out a fire is a מלאכה, so smoking is forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא אָמַר: אָסוּר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמְּכַבֶּה.
phrases.english: Rav Huna said: It is forbidden, because he extinguishes.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא אָמַר: אָסוּר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמְּכַבֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another view that forbids smoking, this time with a reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Smoking is forbidden because it puts out coals.

steps.title: רב נחמן: why not say it is because it lights fire?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks רב הונא why he didn't give lighting a fire as the reason instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: Let the Master say it is forbidden because one lights a fire.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן questions רב הונא's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The spices also make the coals burn stronger, and that counts as lighting a fire. רב נחמן asks why רב הונא named putting out instead of lighting.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to him:
And let the Master say: because he kindles?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן: וְנֵימָא מָר מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמַּבְעִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reason רב הונא gave in Step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's reason that smoking is forbidden because it puts out coals.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Lighting is also part of what happens, so why give putting out as the reason?

steps.title: Both: first it puts out, then it lights
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that both happen: first the coals go out, and later the fire burns more.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: At the start it puts out, and at the end it lights.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers רב נחמן. Both מלאכות are involved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא does not take back his reason. He adds lighting to it. The spices first put out some coals, and then they make the fire burn stronger, so two איסורים are done.

keyTerms.meaning: And at its end; in the end

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב הונא, smoking fruit over coals on יום טוב involves two מלאכות: putting out fire and lighting fire.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Its beginning is extinguishing, and its end is kindling.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: תְּחִלָּתוֹ מְכַבֶּה וְסוֹפוֹ מַבְעִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן's question from Step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both reasons are true at different stages
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only one reason applies, either putting out or lighting.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both happen. First the coals are put out, and then the fire is lit up more.

steps.title: רב יהודה: putting spices on a burning coal is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that putting spices directly on a burning coal on יום טוב is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: On top of a burning coal, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives a ruling about where the spices are placed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His ruling is about spices placed directly on a live coal. That is where the putting out and lighting just discussed actually happen.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
On top of a coal, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: עַל גַּבֵּי גַּחֶלֶת אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a ruling about spices placed directly on a coal, after the discussion of putting out and lighting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Putting spices directly on a burning coal on יום טוב is forbidden.
